title: Lookup malware URL
means: The published REST request is GET https://webrisk.googleapis.com/v1/uris:search?threatTypes=MALWARE&uri=http%3A%2F%2Ftestsafebrowsing.appspot.com%2Fs%2Fmalware.html&key=API_KEY, with the shown JSON response. SearchUris is outside the measured demand; this example does not bring a REST route or authentication flow into scope.

title: Multiple threat types
means: You can specify multiple threat types in a single request by repeating the threatTypes field. The published query fragment is &threatTypes=SOCIAL_ENGINEERING&threatTypes=MALWARE. No URI or response is given for this fragment.

title: No matches
means: If no results match your request, you will get an empty JSON response of {} . This means that the URL you provided isn't on any threat lists.

title: Cache expiration
means: The expireTime field indicates the timestamp at which the match should be considered expired.

title: One URL per request
means: The Lookup API supports one URL per request. To check multiple URLs, you need to send a separate request for each URL.

title: Valid URI without caller canonicalization
means: The URL must be valid (see RFC 2396) but it doesn't need to be canonicalized.

title: Java SearchUri sample
means: The Java sample initializes WebRiskServiceClient, sets uri to http://testsafebrowsing.appspot.com/s/malware.html and threatType to MALWARE, calls searchUris, and prints the threat or that the URL is safe. It supplies no separate JSON response.

title: Python search_uri sample
means: The Python sample constructs SearchUrisRequest with threat_types and uri, calls search_uris and prints the threat or that the URL is safe. Its Args examples name http://testsafebrowsing.appspot.com/s/malware.html and ThreatType.MALWARE; it supplies no separate JSON response.
